compatibility.policy: This registry is the single source of truth for the hand-written SDK layers (transport, session, entitlement, preferences, runtime). It covers what ops/build/sdk-surface.json deliberately does not: the operationId surface is generated for TypeScript and Python only, so the hosted-login and commercial-entitlement behaviour of every published SDK is reconciled here instead. The checker never infers a capability from source; every present entry names the exact file and symbol that provides it, and every missing entry names the wave that will add it. A capability declared as parity must be present in every language, so closing a gap means flipping an entry from missing to present with a real symbol, not relaxing the declaration. Capability entries are append-only in id; changing the file or symbol behind a present entry is a deliberate edit the diff gate can review, and dropping an id or downgrading parity from parity to divergent is a breaking change for the cross-language contract and requires a minor version bump plus a CHANGELOG entry. Adding a language id is allowed and must declare every existing capability for it.

capabilities.summary: The HTTP transport is an injectable seam so a caller can supply retries, proxies, timeouts, or a test double.

python.note: SSOClient calls urllib.request.urlopen directly; hosted_login has no seam either.
python.plan: W4 Transport: introduce a Transport Protocol mirroring FetchLike and route both modules through it.

rust.note: with_http_client takes the concrete reqwest::blocking::Client, so a caller cannot supply an async client.
rust.plan: W4 Transport: replace the HttpClient type alias with an async trait and keep a blocking adapter behind a feature flag.

capabilities.summary: The short-lived login transaction is persisted through a caller-suppliable store so multi-worker deployments are possible.
An in-process state store ships for development and single-process examples.
The current access token is readable without a round trip.
Callers can branch on a usable session without issuing a request.

go.note: Callers compare AccessToken() against the empty string instead.
go.plan: W3 Session: add IsLoggedIn so every language exposes the same predicate.

capabilities.summary: Local token state is dropped without notifying the authorization server.

typescript.note: clearTokens exists but is private and only reached from logout and refresh failure.
typescript.plan: W3 Session: make the local reset reachable, mirroring clear() elsewhere.

python.note: logout() is the only path that drops token state.
python.plan: W3 Session: add clear() so logout and local reset are separable.

capabilities.summary: Ending a session notifies the authorization server so refresh tokens and server-side sessions are revoked, not merely forgotten.

go.note: Only Clear() exists, so a Go caller cannot revoke server-side state.
go.plan: W3 Session: add Logout(ctx) that posts /logout before clearing.

rust.note: clear() drops local state but never revokes; the Rust crate is the only SDK with no server-side logout path.
rust.plan: W3 Session: add logout() posting /logout, keeping clear() for local reset.

capabilities.summary: FeatureKey and LimitKey are typed constants in the SDK so a caller never compares raw strings, mirroring commerce.FeatureKey and commerce.LimitKey.

go.note: W2: AccountContext.Entitlement stays map[string]any for wire compatibility; License and HasFeature add the typed view. Has and Limit reject a key this build does not define, because a string-typed constant alone would still let Feature("anything") be granted.

typescript.note: W2: typed view added alongside the unchanged raw account-context response. hasFeature and limitOf reject a key ALL_FEATURES/ALL_LIMITS does not list, because a plain string parameter would otherwise grant anything the server sent.

python.note: W2: typed view added alongside the unchanged raw account-context dict, so the PyPI surface stays backward compatible.

php.note: W2: typed view added alongside the unchanged raw account-context array. has() and limit() reject a key outside Entitlement::FEATURES/LIMITS, because PHP cannot stop a caller passing an arbitrary string.

rust.note: W2: entitlement is no longer Option<Value>; Feature and Limit are typed and effective() semantics ship with the SDK.

capabilities.summary: A signed commercial entitlement file is verified locally so an air-gapped deployment can gate paid features without a vendor call on the login path.

go.note: W2: crypto/ed25519 is stdlib, so verification is direct rather than injected. A structurally incomplete envelope reports license_malformed, not a zero-valued version, to match the other SDKs.

typescript.note: W2: verification is async so a WebCrypto or @noble/curves verifier can be injected without this package taking a dependency; WebCrypto Ed25519 is still unevenly deployed.

python.note: W2: the package is stdlib-only by design and the stdlib has no Ed25519, so a LicenseVerifier callable is injected (cryptography, PyNaCl, or equivalent) rather than adding a dependency or hand-rolling a signature check.

php.note: W2: a callable verifier is supplied; sodiumVerifier() uses ext-sodium when loaded so the package declares no hard extension requirement.

rust.note: W2: local Ed25519 verification. LicenseTrust::vendor_pinned() reports TrustUnconfigured until a release supplies the vendor root, so no placeholder key ships.
